documents.name: EDO WONDERLAND Nikko Edomura
documents.summary: A full recreated Edo-period town built around role-play, ninja and samurai activities, interactive houses and live entertainment rather than passive historical display.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of Japan’s most convincing historical theme-park experiences and worth substantial regional travel. Some activities cost extra and spoken-Japanese shows lose nuance without the language, but the destination remains strong beyond those components.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: historical theme park · ninja role play

audience.notes: Many signature child role-play activities become strongest around age five and above; adults still have substantial environment, show and activity value.

coverImage.alt: EDO WONDERLAND Nikko Edomura in Nikko, Tochigi.

documents.name: Iwami Tatamigaura
documents.summary: A broad Miocene wave-cut platform whose repeating nodules, potholes and horizontal beds become especially legible at low tide.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for geology and unusual coastlines if timed for low tide and moderate seas. High water hides much of the pattern, so tide planning is part of the recommendation rather than a minor optimisation.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Short physical visit, but travel and tide timing are the real effort.

coverImage.alt: The exposed patterned rock platform of Iwami Tatamigaura at the coast.

documents.name: Miyajimanuma Goose Roost Departure
documents.localName: 宮島沼のマガンねぐら立ち
documents.summary: A small Hokkaido wetland that can become extraordinary when tens of thousands of greater white-fronted geese leave or return to the communal roost around dawn and dusk.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile during the migration peak, usually mid-to-late April and late September to early October. Outside migration it should not consume scarce national travel time. Observe only from designated areas and follow local wildlife guidance.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Easy physical access but high timing discipline: arrive for dawn or dusk in the migration window and observe only from designated areas.

coverImage.alt: A large flock of waterbirds over Miyajimanuma during spring migration.

documents.name: Moriyoshiyama Snow Monsters
documents.summary: One of Japan’s reliable “snow monster” landscapes, where heavily rimed trees form sculptural winter fields reached via the Ani gondola.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile in a good winter weather window, roughly early January to early March. Treat forecast and lift operation as first-class constraints and keep schedule flexibility rather than assuming the phenomenon guarantees visibility on a fixed day.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Moderate physical effort with gondola access, but travel planning should retain a weather-flexible day.

coverImage.alt: Heavily rimed trees forming snow monsters on Mount Moriyoshi in winter.

documents.name: Okuizumo Tatara Cultural Landscape
documents.localName: 奥出雲たたら製鉄・棚田景観
documents.summary: A rural landscape where former iron-sand extraction terrain was deliberately reworked into rice terraces, channels and productive fields.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for landscape/history interests, ideally as a half- or full-day car journey linking a tatara museum or furnace site with the agricultural terrain. Green rice season, harvest gold and autumn all work. The experience is weaker if treated as one viewpoint without context.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Car strongly recommended; half to full day to connect dispersed landscape evidence and interpretation.

coverImage.alt: Terraced rice fields in the Okuizumo cultural landscape.

documents.name: Spa Resort Hawaiians
documents.localName: スパリゾートハワイアンズ
documents.summary: A genuinely destination-scale indoor aquatic resort combining big pools and slides, child water zones, hot-water bathing and permanent Polynesian stage entertainment.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination and one of Japan’s most substantial all-weather aquatic attractions. Summer and holiday crowds, swim logistics and extra-charge activities can materially affect value, but the breadth justifies a dedicated visit for water-loving families and adults.

audience.notes: Very broad family appeal, but individual slides and activities have their own height or participation rules that should be checked before visiting.

coverImage.alt: Indoor water park at Spa Resort Hawaiians in Iwaki, Fukushima.

documents.name: Yoshinogari Historical Park
documents.summary: A vast reconstructed Yayoi-period moated settlement where archaeology is made tangible through buildings, landscape and hands-on ancient-life activities.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination and one of Japan’s strongest experiential archaeological sites. The large outdoor footprint is a virtue in mild weather but becomes a real heat, rain and walking consideration in summer.

audience.notes: School-age children gain the most from the craft and archaeology combination; younger children still have outdoor space but less historical comprehension.

coverImage.alt: Reconstructed northern inner-city gate at Yoshinogari Historical Park in Saga.

documents.name: Yunokuni no Mori
documents.localName: 加賀 伝統工芸村 ゆのくにの森
documents.summary: An unusually substantial craft village where historic buildings, working demonstrations and more than 100 hands-on traditional-craft options share one landscaped site.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination for hands-on culture and one of the strongest multi-craft complexes in Japan. Workshop charges accumulate and not every activity suits every age, but the density and variety make the detour worthwhile.

audience.notes: Workshop suitability varies by craft; school-age children can use the broadest range while adults retain full craft and architecture appeal.

coverImage.alt: Echizen craft building at Yunokuni no Mori in Komatsu, Ishikawa.

documents.name: Awa Odori Kaikan
documents.summary: A year-round home for Tokushima’s Awa Odori where skilled dance performances, a museum and audience participation turn a seasonal festival into an accessible permanent experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An excellent compact cultural experience for visitors who will not be in Tokushima during the main August festival. It is not a full-day destination and spoken explanation is mostly Japanese, but the dance is visually immediate and participation travels well across language barriers.

audience.notes: The visual performance is broadly accessible; very young children may not sustain interest through a full show and museum visit.

coverImage.alt: Awa Odori Kaikan building in Tokushima.

documents.name: Koiwai Farm Makiba-en
documents.summary: A destination-scale working-farm visitor park mixing animals, pasture recreation, tractor rides, food production, heritage interpretation and hands-on making.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good rural family destination and worthwhile regional detour in Iwate, particularly in good weather. Much of the appeal is outdoors and seasonal; individual paid activities and same-day capacities can shape the visit.

audience.notes: Broad family fit, with some workshops or rides carrying their own minimum ages or supervision requirements.

coverImage.alt: Entrance gate of Koiwai Farm Makiba-en in Iwate.

documents.name: Kozagawa River Corridor
documents.summary: A clear-water river journey linking a giant monolith, dense pothole fields, low submersible bridges and forested valley scenery.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong regional discovery because the pieces reinforce each other, but not worth a cross-country journey for one roadside stop alone. Visit in dry stable weather when the river is clear; post-rain turbidity weakens much of the visual appeal.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Half or full day by car; kayaking is optional and dependent on water and operator conditions.

coverImage.alt: The enormous Ichimai-iwa rock wall rising beside the Kozagawa River.

documents.name: Misawa Aviation & Science Museum
documents.localName: 青森県立三沢航空科学館
documents.summary: A large aviation-and-science museum where real aircraft and unusually tactile flight exhibits make the engineering legible rather than merely display it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Very good regional destination for aviation, engineering and hands-on science; worth a meaningful detour in northern Aomori, especially for families. Adults uninterested in aircraft will get less from the trip.

audience.notes: Best from preschool age upward; school-age children can engage with the widest range of interactive science content.

coverImage.alt: Aircraft at Misawa Aviation & Science Museum in Aomori.

documents.name: Namahage Museum & Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum
documents.localName: なまはげ館・男鹿真山伝承館
documents.summary: A museum-and-performance pairing that turns Oga’s Namahage tradition into a vivid encounter with masks, ritual context and a live household demonstration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: One of the strongest permanent ways to experience a living regional folk tradition outside festival dates. The demonstration can be loud and intimidating for sensitive young children, and the folklore museum has limited capacity.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: folk culture museum · live ritual demonstration

audience.notes: The live Namahage visit is intentionally forceful and can frighten sensitive preschoolers; older children and adults get much more cultural context.

coverImage.alt: Wood-and-straw Namahage figures displayed at the Namahage Museum in Oga.

documents.name: Nameratoko Gorge
documents.summary: A long granite gorge of white slabs, clear pools, channels and broad sliding waterfalls in southwest Shikoku.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong regional discovery when approached as a gorge landscape rather than a single waterfall. Dry-to-normal water, warm-season greenery and enough time to walk beyond one viewpoint produce the best reward.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Several hours on the normal gorge outing; guided canyoning is a separate optional activity requiring legitimate operators and suitable conditions.

coverImage.alt: Clear water winding through pale granite slabs in Nameratoko Gorge.

documents.name: Shiroi Koibito Park
documents.summary: A confectionery theme park that earns attraction status through make-your-own sweets, designed factory storytelling and playful indoor/outdoor environments rather than the brand shop alone.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good, easy-to-use Sapporo attraction for families and confectionery fans. It remains brand-heavy, workshops cost extra and production-line visibility can vary with operations, so it is a meaningful detour rather than a Japan-trip anchor.

audience.notes: Preschool and primary-school children are especially well served; hands-on workshop participation depends on the selected course and booking availability.

coverImage.alt: Ishiya Chocolate Factory buildings at Shiroi Koibito Park in Sapporo.

documents.name: Shishigahana Wetland & Nakajimadai Forest
documents.localName: 獅子ヶ鼻湿原・中島台
documents.summary: An intimate Chōkai foothill ecosystem of giant pollarded beeches, abundant cold springs and a globally unusual moss community.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A strong regional discovery rather than a national must-see for everyone. It becomes much more compelling for botany, forest ecology or vernacular woodland-use interests. Stay on boardwalks and marked routes; confirm any damaged or restricted sections before visiting.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Roughly 5 km and 2–3 hours on the normal forest/boardwalk circuit.

coverImage.alt: Dense green forest and wetland scenery at Shishigahana.

documents.name: Tottori Sand Dunes Children’s Kingdom
documents.localName: アイエム電子 鳥取砂丘 こどもの国
documents.summary: A large children-first park beside the dunes combining major outdoor play with woodwork, sand craft and rotating creative activities.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Very good for families with preschool and primary-school children and worth a regional detour when travelling through Tottori. Teens and adults without children have much less reason to make a dedicated trip.

audience.notes: Purpose-built for children. Teen and adult fit is mainly as accompanying family rather than as a standalone attraction.

coverImage.alt: Entrance gate of Tottori Sand Dunes Children’s Kingdom.

documents.name: Yanmar Museum
documents.localName: ヤンマーミュージアム
documents.summary: A challenge-based industrial museum where children operate and simulate agricultural, marine and construction machinery instead of only reading about it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good child-centred industrial discovery and a meaningful detour for families in northern Shiga. Reservation priority and time/content limits on busy days matter, and adults visiting without children may find the experience comparatively lightweight.

audience.notes: Designed especially strongly for children; individual challenges have their own minimum ages, size or supervision rules.

coverImage.alt: Exhibition floor inside Yanmar Museum in Nagahama, Shiga.
